absences: NEI 2019 Cost Competitiveness report (microreactor_lcoe[0] FOAK 140-410 and [1] NOAK 90-330 $/MWh): nei.org returned HTTP 403, so these bands were not checked.

INL/RPT-24-80433 (2024) was not re-fetched. microreactor_lcoe[3] (mass-produced 120-150) and capex mass-produced 6,000 $/kWe were not checked. The 2025 report's NOAK assumes 100 units built, not 10 a year, so its figures are not comparable with the 2024 basis.

incentives.points[0] (45Y/48E for nuclear before 2034, three-year phase-out): no primary statute retrieved. Law-firm summaries disagree on the end year (2035 vs 2036). The cited Morgan Lewis page (July 2025) confirms the wording but is secondary, so no check was written.
displaced_alternatives[2] ($1.50/L diesel breakeven, ScienceDirect) and microreactor_lcoe[4] (Nuclear Business Platform range) were not checked, out of search budget.

Items: no HALEU delivery, enrichment contract, DOE fuel award or loan dated after 2026-11-10 was found. Latest hits were the Centrus Oak Ridge centrifuge shipment (2026-11-02, the Piketon record is already shipped) and the Standard Nuclear and BWXT TRISO deals with Antares and Radiant (Aug and Oct 2026, already shipped).
EDF conditional commitments: the only 2026 loan found is the $17.5B AP1000 commitment (2026-06-23). It covers large reactors, outside the 1-20 MW scope. No microreactor commitment surfaced.

checks.claim: The liquid-metal design is 25% cheaper than the gas-cooled one as a first unit, but only 6% cheaper once both are mass-produced.
checks.evidence: INL/RPT-25-87273 Table 10 gives first-unit LCOE of 330 (liquid-metal) and 410 (gas-cooled) $/MWh. The liquid-metal design is therefore about 20% cheaper (19.5%); the 25% figure is the gas-cooled premium read the other way. Table 11 gives 160 and 170 for mass-produced units, about 6% cheaper, which the shipped text gets right.

checks.review: Overruled 2026-11-12 (main session): the shipped '25% cheaper' is INL's own sentence in RPT-25-87273 ('the LCOE for the FOAK LTMR is 25% cheaper compared to the GCMR'), which is the row's cited quote. The agent's arithmetic is right (330 vs 410 is ~20% cheaper; 25% is the gas-cooled premium), but rewriting the number would contradict the quote it cites. Flagged for a human in the PR body.
